sentences.show: The Polish army gave him a paybook, a rank and a serial number. He was a bear.
In April 1942, Polish soldiers in Iran met a boy with an orphaned bear cub.
A young refugee named Irena talked an officer into buying him.
The soldiers called him Wojtek.
He drank condensed milk from an old vodka bottle.
As he grew, they rewarded him with beer. It became his favourite drink.
He wrestled the men, learned to salute, and slept beside them on cold nights.
Then the army sailed for Italy, on a British ship with one rule. No pets.
So the Poles enlisted him.
Private Wojtek. 22nd Artillery Supply Company.
In 1944, at Monte Cassino, his company hauled shells to the guns.
Wojtek watched the men lift the crates. Then he copied them.
Crates of artillery shells, 45 kilos each. He never dropped one.
Historians still argue. But one British soldier remembered a bear carrying ammunition.
On 18 May, the first flag raised over the ruined monastery was Polish.
Wojtek was made a corporal. His company's new badge: a bear carrying a shell.
After the war, he retired to Edinburgh Zoo.
His old comrades came to visit, and spoke to him in Polish.
And he still answered.
Wojtek never dropped a crate. Don't drop us. Subscribe, and join the company.
